title: From data pipelines to real intelligence
summary: Patterns, lessons and practical insights from moving pipelines toward decisions.

body: Most conversations about AI at work start with the model. Mine usually end up somewhere less glamorous: the pipeline, the schema, the column nobody has validated in years. Working as a data engineer at AEM Energy Solutions has taught me that intelligence is the last layer you build, not the first.
The work that made the AI projects possible was mostly foundation work. Looking back at the past year, it falls into a clear order.

items.title: Make the data trustworthy
items.detail: I built a Data Quality Platform from scratch, from database design to a working proof of concept. It is now the standard for checking upstream and downstream project data, because nothing downstream is better than the data going in.

items.title: Make it fast enough to use
items.detail: We moved from a structured SQL setup to NoSQL so real-time AI inference could keep up, while keeping the data fully consistent across systems.

items.title: Make it labelled
items.detail: Retraining models was blocked by manual labelling, so I automated it: local LLMs through Ollama label the unstructured data, and the refined classification models are deployed on AzureML.

items.title: Make the hard formats readable
items.detail: Engineering drawings arrive as PDFs. Turning them into vectors made it possible to classify technical specifications semantically instead of by hand.

items.title: Make it safe
items.detail: Before rolling out LLMs more widely I wrote the company’s first AI Cybersecurity Procedure, so speed never came at the cost of data privacy.

body: Only after those steps did the “intelligent” parts start to feel reliable: dashboards that people act on, assistants that answer from the right data, and models that can be retrained without a week of preparation.
If there is one lesson, it is this: every shortcut in the pipeline shows up later as a model problem. Build the foundation first, and the intelligence has somewhere solid to stand.
